keyAndScale.primaryKey: A major, established primarily by the guitar solo section since the body of the song is percussion and vocals only

scalesUsed.application: Brian May's guitar solo is built on A minor pentatonic with expressive bends, giving the solo its bluesy, anthemic character
Mixed into the solo for bright, triumphant moments, particularly on the high bends and resolution phrases

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A
scalesUsed.application: The underlying chord movement A-D-A-E fits Mixolydian tonality with the natural seventh (G) appearing in passing

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Mixolydian / Blues-rock hybrid in the solo section; the stomping body is essentially atonal percussion
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: F# minor is the relative minor of A major

mainProgression.description: The guitar only enters for the solo section at the end. The chord progression is a classic rock I-IV-I-V pattern played by Brian May with his signature layered guitar tone.

sectionProgressions.description: The famous stomp-stomp-clap rhythm with no guitar or bass. The entire body of the song is built on the iconic percussion pattern with vocals.
Brian May's blazing guitar solo enters over a I-IV-I-V progression, building from controlled phrases to explosive bends and multi-tracked harmony guitar lines

harmonicFunction: A (I) - Tonic chord anchoring the solo section, providing the triumphant home key
D (IV) - Subdominant lifting the harmony and creating forward motion
E (V) - Dominant chord creating tension before resolving back to A

techniques.name: Stomp-Stomp-Clap Rhythm
techniques.description: The iconic body percussion pattern that forms the entire rhythmic foundation of the song - two foot stomps followed by a hand clap, repeated throughout

notes: Beat 1: Stomp (foot on floor)
Beat 2: Stomp (foot on floor)
Beat 3: Clap (hands together)
Beat 4: Rest (silence)
This pattern repeats for the entire song until the guitar solo
The rhythm is in half-time feel at 81 BPM
sequence: Stand or sit with feet flat on the floor
Stomp your foot firmly on beats 1 and 2
Clap your hands sharply on beat 3
Rest on beat 4 - the silence is as important as the sounds
Maintain this pattern with absolute precision throughout
tips: The power of this rhythm is in its precision and simplicity
Every stomp and clap must be exactly on the beat - use a metronome at 81 BPM
The rest on beat 4 creates the hypnotic, driving feel
In a group, synchronization is everything - listen to others and lock in

techniques.name: Brian May Guitar Solo
techniques.description: The legendary outro guitar solo using the Red Special's distinctive tone with layered harmonies, expressive bends, and pentatonic-based rock phrasing

notes: Solo is played primarily in A minor pentatonic at the 5th and 12th positions
Extensive use of whole-step and one-and-a-half-step bends on the B and high E strings
Brian May uses a sixpence coin as a pick for his unique attack and tone
The solo builds in intensity from deliberate phrases to rapid-fire pentatonic runs
Harmony guitar parts are layered in thirds in the original recording
sequence: Solo enters on the A chord after the final vocal verse
Opens with deliberate, vocal-like bending phrases in A minor pentatonic
Builds through ascending pentatonic runs with increasing speed
Reaches the climax with sustained high bends and vibrato
Resolves on a big A chord to end the song
tips: Focus on the bending intonation - Brian May's bends are always perfectly pitched
Use your ring finger backed by middle and index for strong, controlled bends
Vibrato should be wide and even, applied after the bend reaches pitch
The tone requires a bright, slightly overdriven sound - not heavy distortion
Practice the solo in phrases, not as one continuous run
details.progression: A - D - A - E (solo played over this progression)

techniques.name: Open Chord Accompaniment for Solo Section
techniques.description: Simple open A, D, and E chord strumming that accompanies the guitar solo, providing the harmonic foundation for the climactic ending

notes: A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (standard open A major)
D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (standard open D major)
E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (standard open E major)
Strum with full downstrokes in a steady eighth-note pattern
This is the rhythm guitar part underneath the Brian May solo
sequence: Enter with a big A chord when the guitar section begins
Move to D for two bars
Return to A for two bars
Hit E for the turnaround, then back to A
tips: Keep the strumming steady and powerful - you are the foundation for the solo
Do not try to compete with the lead guitar - stay solid and rhythmic
Full, open chord voicings work best for the big arena sound
The final A chord should ring out fully for the song's conclusion

sections.name: Verse 1 (Stomp Section)
sections.description: Opening verse with the iconic stomp-stomp-clap rhythm, vocals telling the story of a boy. No guitar in this section.
notes: No guitar in this section - purely vocals and body percussion
The stomp-stomp-clap pattern at 81 BPM is the entire musical foundation
Freddie Mercury's vocal commands the space with just the rhythm behind it
Guitarists can stomp and clap along while waiting for their entrance

sections.name: Verse 2 (Stomp Section)
sections.description: Second verse continuing the stomp-stomp-clap with the story of a young man. Still no guitar.
notes: Same percussion pattern continues through the second verse
Vocal intensity builds slightly from the first verse
The repetition of the rhythm creates an increasingly hypnotic effect
Audience participation grows through each verse in live performance

sections.name: Verse 3 (Stomp Section)
sections.description: Third and final verse with the story of an old man, building maximum anticipation for the guitar entrance.
notes: Maximum vocal intensity as the final verse builds to the climax
The tension of three verses without guitar creates enormous anticipation
Freddiethe iconic vocal hookWe will rock you'
This section relies on the restraint of holding back the guitars

sections.name: Guitar Solo / Outro
sections.description: Brian May's legendary guitar solo finally enters - a blazing, emotional tour de force over A-D-A-E that releases all the built-up tension
notes: The guitar entrance is one of rock's greatest dramatic moments
Solo uses A minor pentatonic with major pentatonic inflections
Expressive bends, vibrato, and building intensity throughout
Ends with a massive sustained A chord that rings to silence

guitar.recommended: Brian May Red Special or similar semi-hollow guitar
alternatives: Any guitar with bright single-coil or low-output humbucker pickups
guitar.pickup: All three pickups in phase for the Brian May signature tone; bridge pickup alone for a brighter approximation

amp.recommended: Vox AC30 (the definitive Brian May amp)

effects.distortion: Treble booster (like a Dallas Rangemaster or BSM treble booster) into the Vox AC30 for Brian May's signature crunch tone
effects.delay: Short slapback delay or tape echo for added depth and the layered feel
effects.reverb: Medium hall reverb simulating the multi-tracked layering of the original
effects.other: A sixpence coin was used as a pick by Brian May for his distinctive attack. A heavy, rigid pick can approximate this tone.

beginner.focus: Learn the stomp-stomp-clap rhythm and the basic A-D-E chord shapes for the solo section accompaniment
steps: Master the stomp-stomp-clap rhythm at exactly 81 BPM
Learn the open A, D, and E major chord shapes
Practice strumming A-D-A-E as an accompaniment for the solo section
Play along with the recording, entering at the correct moment

intermediate.focus: Learn the guitar solo melody and basic bending technique
steps: Learn the A minor pentatonic scale at the 5th position
Practice whole-step bends on the B and high E strings
Learn the main solo phrases note-by-note from the recording
Work on connecting phrases with smooth transitions
intermediate.timeEstimate: 3-4 weeks for the solo with proper technique

advanced.focus: Master the complete solo with authentic tone and expressive nuance
steps: Perfect the bending intonation - every bend must hit the exact target pitch
Develop wide, controlled vibrato for sustained notes
Learn the harmony guitar parts for multi-tracked recording
Dial in the Brian May treble booster into AC30 tone
advanced.timeEstimate: 4-6 weeks for a polished, expressive solo performance

commonMistakes: Rushing the stomp-stomp-clap rhythm - it must be precise and unhurried at 81 BPM
Overbending notes in the solo - Brian May's bends are accurate to exact pitches
Using too much distortion for the solo - May's tone is crunchy, not saturated
Entering the guitar too early - the dramatic impact depends on the long percussion buildup
practiceRoutine: Practice the stomp-stomp-clap rhythm with a metronome for 3 minutes
Run through A-D-A-E chord changes for the solo section (3 minutes)
Practice A minor pentatonic bends at the 5th position (5 minutes)
Work on the solo phrases in small sections (10 minutes)
Play through the complete song from stomp to solo finish (3 minutes)
focusAreas: Rhythmic precision of the stomp-stomp-clap pattern
Bending accuracy and vibrato control for the solo
Dynamic building from the quiet percussion to the explosive guitar entrance
Tone control - achieving the bright, singing May guitar sound
metronomeWork: Lock in the body percussion at exactly 81 BPM
Practice chord changes at 81 BPM (this is actually quite slow, so precision matters)
Work on solo phrases at 60 BPM and gradually build to 81 BPM
The slow tempo means every note and bend is exposed - accuracy is paramount
